recipes.name: Quick and Almost-Professional Buttercream Icing
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
3 drops food coloring, or as needed

steps.text: Cream butter in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment until smooth and fluffy.
Gradually beat in confectioners' sugar until fully incorporated.
Add milk and beat for an additional 3 to 4 minutes, adding more confectioners sugar for a stiffer frosting, if desired.
Add food coloring, if using, and beat for 30 seconds until smooth or until desired color is reached.
Use to frost your favorite cakes and cupcakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick and Almost-Professional Buttercream Icing
raw_recipe.description: Our favorite buttercream frosting recipe is creamy and fluffy, can be tinted for any occasion, and is perfect for piping and decorating.

video.description: Your cakes, cupcakes, and cookies deserve the very best buttercream. That's why you should skip the store-bought stuff and make your own buttercream at home. In this video, we'll show you how to make this top-rated recipe, which has more than 1,500 rave reviews from the Allrecipes community, is as good as it gets.

review.reviewBody: I'm a novice cake decorator and this is the first time I've ever in my life reviewed a recipe, but I was so overjoyed I had to do it. I have been trying buttercream recipes for 4 months now, and it's been horrible. I wanted something that did not include the nasty shortening, and was easy to make. I didn't have any luck with any meringue buttercreams either, which just tasted like a big block of butter and requires refrigeration, re-whipping, etc. I was THRILLED to find this recipe! First I made the initial recipe as written, which was a small batch. Then I quadrupled the recipe to make 32 servings to frost/decorate a 9 x 13 layer cake. I found that it's EXTREMELY important to cream the softened butter for several minutes first, then I added the confectioners sugar (after sifting it first) a cup at a time until combined. Then added clear vanilla extract, and for the 4x recipe I only used 1 Tbsp skim milk. Then really important: continue to beat for another 4 minutes! Came out SO fluffy and light and snow white colored. Extremely easy to frost and pipe decorations. Got a nice crust as well. I had several "foodies" taste it and they gave it 2 thumbs up as well. THANK YOU!!!!!

Creamy and fluffy frosting, yet still perfect for piping/decorating. One recipe, however, was barely enough to frost ten cupcakes, so keep this in mind for any of your frosting or decorating needs. I used this for coconut cupcakes, so I flavored it with some coconut oil flavoring, then topped with toasted, shredded coconut. I would call this one of the more exceptional buttercream frosting recipes.

This is a great buttercream icing recipe. I followed it fairly closely, thought I did add extra vanilla, which then necessitated adding some extra 10X sugar to make up for the extra liquid. It does not make all that much, so I will prob double it when decorating a cake. It made enough for me to not-over-generously ice 18 cupcakes. Great taste and consistency. GO BULLDOGS! ;) TY for a great recipe!

I was a little disappointed with this icing when I first made it. It was good and easy, but there was just a little lacking in terms of flavor. I made it again and this time used salted butter instead of unsalted (as a previous reviewer suggested), doubled the vanilla (previous reviewer again), and used evaporated milk (next time I might try cream, but I didn't have that on hand) instead of regular milk. I used extra sugar to compensate for the extra vanilla and the thin texture it had the first time (don't want to reduce the milk because I needed every drop of frosting) and it was perfect. I doubled the recipe and it was just enough to frost a 3-layer cake. I'm giving the original recipe 4 stars.

This is the best buttercream I've ever tasted. My recipe is close, but the extra vanilla puts it well over the top. I used salted butter, and added a little pinch of salt which I think helps balance out the flavors a bit. Amazing texture, perfection.

Professional baker here. A few tips...add salt! This recipe does not call for it but you NEED salt to balance out the sweetness. If your recipe was too sweet and sugary, it’s because you need to add to salt. I added 3/4 of a teaspoon of table salt to my recipe and it was delicious. If you want nice fluffy buttercream, switch to a whip attachment at the end and whip for five minutes! This is crucial for fluffiness.

This was a great recipe for a fluffier, creamy buttercream. It does, however, need salt. Most buttercreams call for some salt and this was too sweet without it. I multiplied this recipe 6.5 times for 55 cupcakes (had lots leftover) and added about 1 tsp of salt and cut the milk in half. It had a great flavor and was the right consistency for piping cupcakes. I did put them in the fridge to set a bit before serving as it was a bit soft. There were lots of compliments and most people ate more than one. Will definitely use again. Will probably add food coloring before milk, and may use a little less milk than I did, for a slightly thicker result.

I learned buttercream from my mom. Use salted butter that's cold. Freeze a metal bowl. Do not add all the liquid at once, drizzle until the consistency suits you, and sift your powdered sugar. Buttercream is easy but temperamental. Your ambient temperature, humidity level, and elevation will impact your results. Take your time and beat the butter like it's the devil himself in church.

This recipe is a good start but it definitely needs a few changes. It is way too sweet and I decreased the sugar by 1/4 cup. I also added cocoa to make it chocolate buttercream. I added 3 tbsp very good unsweetened cocoa along with 1 tbsp instant espresso. You can't really taste the espresso; it just brings out the chocolate flavor more and I added it to the milk so it dissolves before you add it to the butter and sugar. I also used an extra tbsp for a total of 3 tbsp of milk for a smoother texture. If it gets a little to runny, just add a little more powder sugar to stiffen it. Also, be sure to sift both the powder sugar and cocoa.

I’m 79 years old and have been making this frosting since I was 10 years old. I’ve always used salted butter and also add a dash or two of more salt to cut the sweetness. About 15 years ago I discovered Mexican vanilla and that’s the only vanilla I use in my kitchen. Mix cocoa with your powdered sugar for chocolate frosting. I always save a little chocolate frosting and spread it on graham crackers for a quick snack. Even now, when my brother and sister visit, they ask for my chocolate frosted buttercream graham crackers. You can eat them plain or add chopped nuts, coconut, chocolate or white chocolate chips or anything else you enjoy. This buttercream recipe gives a whole new taste to Graham crackers. My adult son stopped by as I was writing this review and asked if I had time to whip up some chocolate frosted graham crackers for him to take home. He’s in the kitchen now setting out the ingredients for me to make the buttercream. (And of course I’ll keep some of them for myself!)😋

Excellent! It's EXTREMELY important to cream the softened butter for several minutes first, then I added the confectioners sugar (after sifting it first) a cup at a time until combined. Then added vanilla extract, and 2 tsp milk. Then really important: continue to beat for another 4 minutes! Came out SO fluffy, light, and not too sweet.
I use this recipe every time I need vanilla buttercream! Great for piping, decorating, and basically anything. Highly recommend!

Not good at all. All it taste like is icing sugar. I followed this recipe exactly and only used the 2cups of icing sugar. I added more butter to try and salvage it. Will never make again. Apparently this recipe is considered American Buttercream. I won't makebthat mistake again. But to my meringues ( swiss, italian, etc) they are much much better. If you do make this, please add salt and beat for at least 5mins
It was amazing, worked perfectly

I was looking for a frosting recipe I could turn into a cherry frosting for butter cupcakes. I used this recipe.i substituted almond extract for the vanilla, used juice from a jar of maraschino cherries instead of the milk and added a few drops of food coloring. It was delicious! A big hit for the birthday party!

My son wanted cookie sandwiches to take to school to share with his class for his birthday. I made this buttercream to use as the filler and it was fantastic! I beat the butter with the paddle beater until it was a fluffy cloud, then added the remaining ingredients as the recipe states, then used the whisk attachment to beat it some more. After three minutes, it still tasted like butter and sugar, by which I mean it looked just right but the flavors had not merged. I added 1/2 tsp of salt and beat it for about four more minutes on medium speed and it was perfect! That extra time made the flavors really come together to reach buttercream perfection, in taste and texture. My son loved them, his class loved them, and I sent the extras to work with my husband. He came home and said they were all gone in minutes and one of his coworkers said it was the best cookie he had ever eaten! I wouldn't tell this to anybody it you guys, but I had too much to do to make the cookies from scratch, so I got them at HEB grocery store here in Texas, which always has really high-quality prepared sweets. The buttercream took the store-bought cookies from really good to magical!
Very quick and easy
This was my first time making buttercream icing. I don’t have a stand mixer and couldn’t find all of my hand mixer so I did it by hand. It took a little time but turned out amazing! Thanks so much!
it did not work i used everything the same and it just curdled.

Just made this and it turned out great - a little sweet for my taste, but definitely worth making again. This is the first time I've made frosting since high school (1970s!) Home Ec class and it is SO easy. I'd recommend for anyone trying to get their kid in to baking because it is that easy and is obviously very rewarding! Also, I used the 1X recipe and it was plenty for a 9X13 Bob's Red Mill chocolate mix cake (I replaced the water in the cake recipe with coffee and a shot of vanilla.) Bookmarked!
